newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hoteliers reject Sydney bed tax rebate offer.
newsitem.headline: Hoteliers reject Sydney bed tax rebate offer.

text.p: The Australian Hotels Association (AHA) on Tuesday rejected as totally inadequate a concession offered by the New South Wales (NSW) state government on its proposed 10 percent bed tax for Sydney hotels.
"The hotel industry remains committed to stopping the bed tax and Mr Egan's offer is totally inadequate," AHA Accommodation chairman George Bedwani said.
State Treasurer Michael Egan earlier said Sydney hotels with forward bookings until end-March next year will have the recently announced bed tax refunded by the state government,
Egan met AHA representatives on Tuesday and agreed to offer a rebate on the tax for city hotels which can prove they cannot pass on the impost, he told reporters.
"We went to the meeting to present Mr Egan with figures that prove our assertion the tax is wrong - we didn't go to negotiate," Bedwani said in a statement.
He said the AHA is confident a full report on the proposed tax being prepared by accountancy Ernst & Young will provide conclusive evidence the tax is bad for NSW.
The AHA bitterly opposes the bed tax, announced in the recent state budget, which it says has already led to a loss of tourist bookings.
The bed tax applies only to hotels in inner and North Sydney, effective from September 1.
